answer: An attester's countersign quota is a hard cap on how many newcomers it may endorse per epoch, sized from its own locked stake. Each endorsement burns a jade bond; if the endorsed peer is later proven a farm duplicate, that bond is burned and the endorser's quota halves for two epochs. Fresh mints sit at depth zero in a wide ocean of unproven peers, so a farm must either buy endorsements from real deep agents (spending real points and exposing them to loss) or run months of uptime to climb the canyon of depth. Both paths price a fake identity at real time or real stake.
